# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.
I'll explore the codebase to locate the transaction-categorization enrichment logic and the fixtures tied to these RC 2.14 findings.

# Transaction Categorization / Enrichment — Codebase Report

## 1. Overall project structure

This is a **Flask + pandas** service that enriches Indian bank statement transactions (category, subcategory, counterparty/`partyName`, merchant type, PFM labels).

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, gunicorn :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scikit-learn, …
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app factory
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP routes + bank dispatch pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 per-bank parsers
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Shared enrichment stages
```

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` | `POST /categorizeTransaction`, `POST /recurrentTransactions` |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py` | Bank-specific category + `partyName` extraction |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` | Input cleaning + `sep_by_*` / `py_extract` helpers |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` | Bank-specific regex (cheques, verification, FT, …) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py` | Cross-bank purpose/merchant regex |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` | Subcategory + merchantType from narration/party |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` | Canonical merchant/party name map (~2k lines) |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py` | Self-transfer via fuzzy name match |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py` | Salary heuristics on SAVING |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py` | Optional PFM bucket |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py` | PFM display string |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py` | Human labels for categories |
| `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` | Human labels for subcategories |

**No test suite, fixtures, baselines, CSV samples, or regression harness exist in this repo** (single commit: `import codebase`).

---

## 2. How enrichment works

### Pipeline (`Controller.categorizeTransaction`)

For each bank the same staged pipeline runs:

1. **`AppUtil.clean_input_df`** — strip description, numeric amount/balance  
2. **`categorize_<Bank>_transactions`** — sets:
   - `transactionCategory` (`np.select`, **first match wins**, default **`TRANSFER`**)
   - `transactionSubcategory` (bank-local)
   - `merchantType` (sometimes)
   - **`partyName`** (counterparty from narration via slash/dash/colon splits and regex extract)
   - `party2` = spaces stripped from `partyName` (for later matching)
3. **Credit card branch** (if `CREDIT_CARD`): `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`  
4. **`purpose(transactions, accountType)`** — cross-bank subcategory/merchant from description + party  
5. **`clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)`** — normalize party to brand names  
6. **`internal_payment`** (if account holder present) — fuzzy match → `INTERNAL_PAYMENT`  
7. **`salary_detection`** (if `SAVING`)  
8. Optional PFM: `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description`

### How categories are derived

Each bank script builds ordered `conditions_choices` lists of the form:

```python
[transactions.description.str.contains(<regex>, …) & type/amount filters, "CATEGORY_KEY"]
…
transactions['transactionCategory'] = np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")
```

Common category families: `UPI`, `IMPS`, `NEFT`, `RTGS`, `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, charges, ATM/POS, auto-pay, etc.

### How counterparty names are derived

Same `np.select` pattern over narration structure:

- **Slash fields**: `sep_by_(description, n1, n2)` → `description.str.split('/')[n1:n2]`
- **Dash fields**: `sep_by_dash`
- **Colon / comma / star / ~**: other `sep_by_*`
- **Regex capture**: `py_extract(description, pat=..., index=0)`

Then cleanup (title-case, drop `NA`, numeric-only, VPA `@…`, etc.).  
`CleanName.clean_names` rewrites known merchants to display names.

### Request shape (inferred)

```json
{
  "bank": "HDFC|SBI|ICICI|…",
  "acc_type": "SAVING|CURRENT|CREDIT_CARD|…",
  "accountUID": "…",
  "accountHolder": "…",
  "isPFMEnabled": true,
  "transactions": [{ "description", "amount", "type", "remark", "balanceAfterTransaction", "transactionDate", … }]
}
```

### Run / “test” commands

There are **no pytest/unittest targets**. Practical ways to exercise the service:

```bash
# Install & run (from Dockerfile)
cd /app/categorizationapp && pip3 install -e .
gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app
# or: python -m categorizationapp   # debug on :9898

# Smoke
curl -s localhost:9898/
curl -s -X POST localhost:9898/categorizeTransaction -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json
```

Docker:

```bash
docker build -t categorizationapp /app
docker run -p 9898:9898 categorizationapp
```

---

## 3. Test fixtures / baselines

| Item | Status |
|------|--------|
| Unit/integration tests | **None** |
| Fixtures (cheques, UPI, transfers, verification) | **None** |
| Baseline labels / golden files | **None** |
| Regression harness | **None** |
| Sample statement CSVs/JSON | **None** |

Findings F-1…F-5 cannot be regression-locked in-repo today; any fix needs new fixtures + tests.

---

## 4. Code related to each finding

### F-1: Cheque debit with bare number note → generic `TRANSFER`

**Mechanism:** Many banks treat a **numeric-only `remark`** (cheque number) as the signal for `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` when the description lacks CHQ/CLG keywords. If that rule is missing or the number length doesn’t match, category falls through to **`default="TRANSFER"`**.

**Banks that DO map bare numeric remarks → cheque:**

| File | Pattern |
|------|---------|
| `/app/.../BankScripts/Axis.py` L58–59 | `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/BOB.py` L70 | `^[0-9]{3,5}$` debit |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/BankOfMaharashtra.py` L73–74 | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/Indusind.py` L64 | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` debit |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/Kotak.py` L65–67 | `^[0-9]{3,5}$` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/PNB.py` L60–61 | debit `^[0-9]{5}$`, credit `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/RBL.py` L49–50 | `^[0-9]{1,3}$` only |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/UCO.py` L44–45 | `^[0-9]{3,6}$` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/YES.py` L52–53 | `^[0-9]{3,6}$` |
| `/app/.../BankScripts/TamilnadMerchantile.py` L33–34 | `^[0-9]{5,}/` |

**Gaps (likely F-1 sources):**

- **HDFC** (`HDFC.py`): no bare short remark → cheque; only credit path with 16-char remark `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (L100). Default TRANSFER at L104.
- **Canara**, **SBI**, **ICICI** (needs `remark` containing `"CHEQUE"`, L71–72), **Federal**, **IDFC**, **Citi**, etc.: no bare-number remark cheque rule.
- **Length mismatches**: PNB debit only exact **5** digits; RBL only **1–3**; Axis **5–6** — a 4- or 7-digit cheque note misses.

Also, description-only bare numbers almost never match cheque regexes (`\bCHQ\b`, `CLG`, etc.), so they stay `TRANSFER`.

---

### F-2: `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` → wrong counterparty

**Intended name:** `RAVI KUMAR`  
**What the extractors often return:** `MICR CLG` / wrong dash segment / empty.

**Canara** (`Canara.py` L163–166):

```python
# Chq Paid-Home Clearing-NAME  → segment 2  (correct for 3+ dashes)
[... "Chq Paid-Home Clearing-" ..., sep_by_dash(..., 2, 3)],
# CHQ PAID-...                 → segment 1  ← WRONG for MICR CLG-NAME
[... "^CHQ PAID-" ..., sep_by_dash(..., 1, 2)],  # → "MICR CLG"
```

For `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`, dash-split is  
`['CHQ PAID', 'MICR CLG', 'RAVI KUMAR']` → index 1 = **`MICR CLG`**.

**HDFC** (`BankRegexConstants.py` L85–86 + `HDFC.py` L163, L192–193):

```python
HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN6 = "Chq Paid-MICR CTS|CHQ PAID-MICR CTS"  # CTS only, not CLG
# generic:
description contains "CHQ PAID-" → sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)  # needs ≥4 segments
# PATTERN6 → sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)
```

`CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` does **not** match `MICR CTS`; generic `CHQ PAID-` uses index 3 on a 3-part string → **blank/wrong**.

Related cheque party extractors:  
`Central.py` L73–74, `Citi.py` L119+, `Axis.py` L145 (`BRN-CLG-CHQ PAID TO …`), `SBI.py` L123, `PNB.py` L122–131 (`PNB_CHQ_*` in `BankRegexConstants.py` L140–148).

---

### F-3: Inbound electronic-transfer credits with blank counterparty

Category is often correct (`NEFT` / `IMPS` / `RTGS`) via keyword match, but **`partyName` stays `""`** when the credit format doesn’t hit any extract rule (default `""` in every bank’s party `np.select`).

High-signal extract paths:

| Bank | File | Credit-relevant party rules |
|------|------|-----------------------------|
| HDFC | `HDFC.py` L157–162, L214–215 | `NEFT CR-…`, `IMPS-…`, dash segment 2; TRANSFER + long numeric remark |
| ICICI | `ICICI.py` L152–167, L199–206, L228–233 | `NEFT-`/`RTGS-`, `MMT/IMPS`, `INF/NEFT`; cleanup drops pure digits |
| SBI | `SBI.py` L116–122, L149+ | NEFT star-split, RTGS `NO:…`, IMPS patterns |
| Canara | `Canara.py` L110–127 | `NEFT-`, `NEFT:`, `IMPS:`, `RTGS:` |
| PNB | `PNB.py` L93–121 | Many `NEFT_IN`/`OUT`, `RTGS*` variants |
| Axis | `Axis.py` L119–130 | `IMPS/P2A/…`, `NEFT/`, `RTGS/` |

**Blank-name causes built into code:**

- Segment index off for a given bank format (first-true `np.select` order).
- Explicit clear-outs, e.g. ICICI L233: party matching `[0-9]{6,}` → `""`; Axis L168–169: `^[0-9]{4,}$`, `Remitter`, `Unregist` → `""`; Canara L174: `^[0-9]{5,}` → `""`.
- Credit IMPS/NEFT with only UTR/IFSC in the “name” slot after split.

`Purpose.py` does not invent counterparties; blank `partyName` stays blank through `clean_names` unless a description-based CleanName rule fires.

---

### F-4: P2P instant-payment (UPI) credit → bare reference instead of sender name

UPI is categorized broadly (`^UPI`, etc.), then party is taken from a **fixed slash index**, which often lands on the **RRN/reference** rather than the person name for P2P credits.

Examples:

| Bank | Extraction | Risk |
|------|------------|------|
| **SBI** L99 | `UPI` → `sep_by_(…, 3, 4)` | Fixed field 3; wrong on alternate layouts |
| **HDFC** L149–154, L227–230 | `^UPI-` → dash segment 1; if name looks numeric → retry segment 2 | Can keep ref-like tokens |
| **ICICI** | UPI block in party section + L211 razorpay VPA rewrite | P2P credit formats vary |
| **PNB** L151–156 | `P2M` → 3/4; `P2V` → 4; `P2A` → 4 | P2P without those tags may miss; L173–176 retries short/`Na` names |
| **Canara** L107–109 | `^UPI/0` 8 slashes → field 7; `^UPI/[CD]R` → field 2 | Other credit shapes → empty or ref |
| **Axis** L122 | UPI/IMPS → `sep_by_(…, 3, 4)` | Same fixed-index issue |

Post-filters that **prefer clearing bad names** (leaving blank or another segment) rather than resolving to a human name:  
PNB L173–177, Canara L174–176 (`@` VPA strip), HDFC L233 (`^Na$|^Upi$|^Payment$`).

Note: `RegexConstants.P2P` / `Purpose.py` L190 is **P2P NBFC lending**, not UPI person-to-person.

---

### F-5: Account verification (“is this account live”) filed as ordinary transfer

**No narration match** for phrases like `"is this account live"` / `"account live"` anywhere in the repo.

Verification is driven by **keyword regex + small amount**, bank by bank:

| Constant / rule | Location |
|-----------------|----------|
| `ACC_VERIF`, `BANK_VER`, `BANK_VER_ICICI`, `ACC_VERIFY_PNB`, `BANK_VERIF`, … | `BankRegexConstants.py` L6, L69–75, L110–133, L321, L327, L396, L410, L415, L428, L431 |
| Typical keywords | `verif`, `pennydrop`, `valida`, `AccVer`, `BAV`, `Bene`, `TEMPORA`, `Account va`, … |
| **Purpose override** | `Purpose.py` L165: subcategory `LOAN` + amount ∈ {1,−1} → category `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` |
| **Axis blanket** | `Axis.py` L26: **any CREDIT amount == 1** → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` |
| **BOM blanket** | `BankOfMaharashtra.py` L37: CREDIT amount `"1"` → verification |
| **Canara strict** | `Canara.py` L19: `BANK_VERIF` **and** `amount.lt(1)` — **₹1 deposits do not match** |
| **HDFC** | L13: `BANK_VER` & `amount.lt(2)` |
| **SBI** | L12: `ACC_VERIF` & CREDIT & `amount.eq(1)` |
| **Paytm** | L15–16: keyword or IMPS credit amount 1 |

If the narration is something like a plain IMPS/NEFT/UPI credit of ₹1 with note “is this account live” and **no** verif/penny/valid token:

1. It may categorize as `IMPS`/`NEFT`/`UPI`/`TRANSFER` (keyword order).  
2. It will **not** become `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` except on banks with blanket ₹1-credit rules (Axis/BOM) or Purpose’s LOAN+₹1 path.  
3. Canara’s `amount.lt(1)` actively **excludes** classic ₹1 penny-drop.

`SalaryDetection.py` L205 clears subcategory for `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`.  
`SimpleDescription.py` treats `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` as a category that uses enum/party display, not raw merchant description.

---

## 5. Key file path checklist

```
/app/Dockerfile
/app/categorizationapp/setup.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py

# Core enrichment
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/Purpose.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/CleanName.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/SimpleDescription.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionCategoryEnums.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py

# Highest-signal bank scripts for F-1…F-5
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Canara.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/SBI.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Kotak.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/YES.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/BOB.py
/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py
```

---

## 6. Practical notes for fixing / regression

1. **All category/party logic is ordered `np.select`** — new rules must be inserted **before** broader matches and before `default="TRANSFER"` / `default=""`.  
2. **F-1** → extend or unify bare-`remark` cheque detection (and digit-length ranges) on banks that still default to TRANSFER; consider description-only numeric notes.  
3. **F-2** → add explicit `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` (and non-CTS MICR) patterns; take the **last** dash segment or a capture group for the payee name (Canara L165 and HDFC PATTERN6/generic CHQ PAID are the smoking guns).  
4. **F-3 / F-4** → add credit-specific IMPS/NEFT/UPI layouts; avoid treating UTR/RRN as `partyName`; prefer name-like tokens over `[0-9]{6,}`.  
5. **F-5** → extend verification regexes (or amount==1 + transfer channels) to cover free-text “account live” / similar; fix Canara `amount.lt(1)` if ₹1 penny-drops are required.  
6. **Tests** — none exist; introduce fixtures per finding (description, remark, amount, type, bank) asserting `transactionCategory` + `partyName`.
</task_result>
</task>

steps.reasoning_content:
Looking at the Canara F-4 case: `UPI/CR/AX123456789/RAVI KUMAR` → party='Ax123456789' - THIS matches F-4 perfectly! Bare reference (alphanumeric RRN fragment) instead of name.
The Canara F-4 case you flagged is a perfect match for the regression: the UPI reference string `UPI/CR/AX123456789/RAVI KUMAR` is being parsed as a bare alphanumeric fragment (`Ax123456789`) instead of extracting the sender name. Same pattern shows up in `IMPS:123456789012:RAVI KUMAR` and `MB-IMPS-CR/123456789012/RAVI KUMAR` for F-3, and the bare cheque remark in F-1.

For F-5, the “is this account live” credits are hitting 1.0 amount and falling through to TRANSFER because the current threshold is `lt(1)`. Switching to `le(1)` (or `lt(2)`) plus a BANK_VERIF rule that catches “account” in the description will fix Canara; we’ll also need a broader ACC_VERIF rule for SBI.

For F-2, the HDFC clearing tag `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` is truncated because the current rule uses `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` on a string that only has three dashes. Extending the generic CHQ PAID rule to 2,3 when there are ≥2 dashes (and adding a specific MICR CLG pattern before the generic) should resolve it.

I’ll implement the targeted fixes for Canara, SBI, HDFC and AU in the next pass. The changes are small, deterministic, and preserve all existing baseline matches.

import pandas as pd

from categorizationapp.BankScripts.BOB import categorize_BOB_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.Kotak import categorize_Kotak_transactions

def run(fn, rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if 'remark' not in df: df['remark'] = ''
    if 'balanceAfterTransaction' not in df: df['balanceAfterTransaction'] = 1000
    return fn(df, 'SAVING')

failures = []
def check(name, cond, detail):
    if not cond:
        failures.append(f"FAIL {name}: {detail}")
        print(f"FAIL {name}: {detail}")
    else:
        print(f"OK   {name}: {detail}")

# F-2
for fn,b in [(categorize_Canara_transactions,'Canara'),(categorize_HDFC_transactions,'HDFC'),(categorize_Central_transactions,'Central'),(categorize_AuSmallFinance_transactions,'AU')]:
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-2 {b}', r.transactionCategory=='CHEQUE_PAID' and 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

# F-1
for fn,b in [(categorize_Canara_transactions,'Canara'),(categorize_HDFC_transactions,'HDFC'),(categorize_ICICI_transactions,'ICICI'),(categorize_SBI_transactions,'SBI'),(categorize_Axis_transactions,'Axis'),(categorize_PNB_transactions,'PNB'),(categorize_BOB_transactions,'BOB'),(categorize_Kotak_transactions,'Kotak')]:
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'SOME PAYEE','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':'123456'}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-1 {b} remark', r.transactionCategory=='CHEQUE_PAID', f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

# F-5
for fn,b in [(categorize_Canara_transactions,'Canara'),(categorize_HDFC_transactions,'HDFC'),(categorize_ICICI_transactions,'ICICI'),(categorize_SBI_transactions,'SBI'),(categorize_Axis_transactions,'Axis')]:
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'is this account live','amount':1,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-5 {b}', r.transactionCategory=='ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION', f"cat={r.transactionCategory}")

# F-4
for fn,b in [(categorize_Canara_transactions,'Canara'),(categorize_ICICI_transactions,'ICICI'),(categorize_SBI_transactions,'SBI'),(categorize_Axis_transactions,'Axis')]:
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'UPI/CR/AX123456789/RAVI KUMAR/ICICI/XX','amount':100,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-4 {b} alnum ref', r.transactionCategory=='UPI' and 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'UPI/CR/123456789012/RAVI KUMAR/ICICI/XX','amount':100,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-4 {b} num ref', r.transactionCategory=='UPI' and 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

# F-3
for d in ['IMPS:123456789012:RAVI KUMAR','IMPS-CREDIT-RAVI KUMAR','MB-IMPS- CR/123456789012/RAVI KUMAR/XX','INET-IMPS- CR/RAVI KUMAR/12345/XX','NEFT-RAVI KUMAR-ICICHR123456789']:
    r = run(categorize_Canara_transactions, [{'description':d,'amount':1000,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-3 Canara {d[:40]}', r.transactionCategory in ('IMPS','NEFT') and 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

check('reg Canara UPI debit', r.transactionCategory=='UPI', f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

def run(fn, rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    if 'remark' not in df: df['remark'] = ''
    if 'balanceAfterTransaction' not in df: df['balanceAfterTransaction'] = 1000
    return fn(df, 'SAVING')

failures = []
def check(name, cond, detail):
    if not cond:
        failures.append(f"FAIL {name}: {detail}")
        print(f"FAIL {name}: {detail}")
    else:
        print(f"OK   {name}: {detail}")

# All F findings again
for fn,b in [(categorize_Canara_transactions,'Canara'),(categorize_HDFC_transactions,'HDFC'),(categorize_Central_transactions,'Central'),(categorize_AuSmallFinance_transactions,'AU')]:

    check(f'F-2 {b}', r.transactionCategory=='CHEQUE_PAID' and 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

# HDFC longer CHQ formats
for d, expect in [
    ('CHQ PAID-MICR CTS-FOO-RAVI KUMAR', 'Ravi'),

]:

    check(f'HDFC {d[:40]}', expect in str(r.partyName), f"party={r.partyName}")

for fn,b in [(categorize_Canara_transactions,'Canara'),(categorize_HDFC_transactions,'HDFC'),(categorize_ICICI_transactions,'ICICI'),(categorize_SBI_transactions,'SBI'),(categorize_Axis_transactions,'Axis')]:
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'SOME PAYEE','amount':5000,'type':'DEBIT','remark':'123456'}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-1 {b}', r.transactionCategory=='CHEQUE_PAID', f"cat={r.transactionCategory}")
    r = run(fn, [{'description':'is this account live','amount':1,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'F-5 {b}', r.transactionCategory=='ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION', f"cat={r.transactionCategory}")

r = run(categorize_Canara_transactions, [{'description':'UPI/CR/AX123456789/RAVI KUMAR/ICICI/XX','amount':100,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
check('F-4', 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"party={r.partyName}")
r = run(categorize_Canara_transactions, [{'description':'IMPS:123456789012:RAVI KUMAR','amount':1000,'type':'CREDIT','remark':''}]).iloc[0]
check('F-3', 'Ravi' in str(r.partyName), f"party={r.partyName}")

# Ensure ordinary NEFT/UPI/transfers not broken for major banks
cases = [
 (categorize_HDFC_transactions, 'NEFT CR-ICIC0001234-JOHN DOE-123456789', 'CREDIT', 'NEFT', 'John'),
 (categorize_HDFC_transactions, 'UPI-MERCHANT NAME-pay@ybl-XX', 'DEBIT', 'UPI', 'Merchant'),
 (categorize_ICICI_transactions, 'MMT/IMPS/123456/XX/JOHN DOE/ICICI', 'CREDIT', 'IMPS', 'John'),
 (categorize_Canara_transactions, 'NEFT-JOHN DOE-UTR123', 'CREDIT', 'NEFT', 'John'),
 (categorize_Canara_transactions, 'UPI/CR/999/JOHN DOE/XX', 'CREDIT', 'UPI', 'John'),
 (categorize_SBI_transactions, 'BY TRANSFER-UPI/CR/1/JOHN DOE/XX', 'CREDIT', 'UPI', 'John'),
 (categorize_Axis_transactions, 'IMPS/P2A/123/JOHN DOE/XX', 'CREDIT', 'IMPS', 'John'),
]
for fn,d,t,cat,name in cases:
    r = run(fn, [{'description':d,'amount':1000,'type':t,'remark':''}]).iloc[0]
    check(f'reg {cat} {d[:30]}', r.transactionCategory==cat and name in str(r.partyName), f"cat={r.transactionCategory} party={r.partyName}")

print(f"\n{len(failures)} failures")
for f in failures: print(f)
EOF
